scope.initialization: host explicitly runs init_ingress_replay_ledger.mjs once; existing files cannot be reset

proof_state.accepted_claims: append-only logical sequence of nonce, revision and signed-claim SHA-256 records
proof_state.current_revision: highest committed revision for exact source, host subject and slot
proof_state.readiness: WASM ingress ready plus in-session signed coverage; run and verify reread the durable record
proof_state.replay_window: at most 50000 accepted claims, retained across process restarts without eviction
proof_state.execution_receipts: optional durable host-observed WASM run records with monotonic sequence and claim-count anchors; v1 history is readable and new v2 records bind an exact multi-input ProgramBundle byte digest
proof_state.state_handoffs: optional content-addressed links from a parent receipt output to a later signed state claim, recorded atomically with that claim
proof_state.retained_checkpoints: private host-owned files named by committed receipt ID, containing the exact ProgramBundle bytes and manifest; restore verifies both digests against the same-subject receipt
proof_state.checkpoint_restores: durable host restore events anchor an exact receipt, manifest, checkpoint digest and execution order; descendant receipts name their immediate state parent and restore event
proof_state.failure: corrupt, missing, mismatched-subject or untrusted ledger closes execution; no automatic reset

valid_transitions: host explicitly initializes the ledger before runner startup; missing or deleted ledger fails closed
host loads policy and ledger, validates owner, file mode, schema and exact subject
verified signed claim checks nonce and monotonic revision against the ledger
native bind succeeds before a new claim is committed; if commit fails, the bound tensor is cleared
commit obtains an exclusive filesystem lock and rechecks replay state across processes
commit writes a complete private snapshot to a new file, fsyncs, atomically renames and fsyncs the parent directory
run and verify hold the ledger lock while checking all bound claims and executing the WASM reference
durable run appends an execution receipt under the same lock before returning success
durable run fsyncs its bounded checkpoint into the private store before committing the receipt; receipt commit failure removes its new checkpoint
receipt-bound restore stages a fresh graph and manifest only after checking the retained bytes and receipt; input tensors and signed proofs must be bound again
restore commits its event under the exclusive ledger lock before replacing the live session; a failed event commit preserves the prior session
a failed run after numerical execution starts discards the current session; it cannot publish a descendant receipt from uncommitted mutable state
state bind checks exact parent receipt output bytes and atomically appends its signed claim plus a handoff record
later execution receipt input records reference the handoff ID; each subject/source/logical-port/branch lane must advance parent receipt sequence
clear removes session coverage but never erases durable nonce or revision history
limits: Ledger storage is a host trust root; a privileged writer can rewrite its history because the file is not independently authenticated.
The ledger parent must be host-owned and not group/world writable, and the ledger file must be private to the runner user.
A process crash may leave a lock directory; only an operator who has verified no runner owns it may recover it.
50,000 accepted claims or a 32 MiB ledger file fails closed rather than silently discarding replay history.
50,000 execution receipts or 50,000 state handoffs fail closed; pre-receipt ledger snapshots remain readable without resetting claim history.
Retained ProgramBundle bytes are limited to 8 MiB per receipt and 512 MiB per store; a crash can leave an unreferenced checkpoint requiring host cleanup.
Older v2 receipts without retained checkpoint files remain readable but cannot be restored.
Older receipts without a state-parent or restore event remain readable; their absent ancestry is never inferred.
At most 50,000 restore events may be recorded; their record bytes count toward the ledger size cap.
The JSON snapshot is rewritten for each commit; this is a reference-machine persistence contract, not a high-throughput database.
Signing verifies the configured issuer's claim, not the truth of an external observation; direct WASM callers bypass the Node host gate.
